ratings.note: Suggested 4; lowered to 3 because the confirm page showed the details one step earlier and an SMS reminder arrives the evening before, so a wrong-time or wrong-vehicle arrival is possible but not the usual result.

Screenshot confirms an unlabelled Few-left block above Morning on every day view; each slot still shows its time, so it mostly slows scanning, but the visual order and the DOM order differ for screen-reader users who also look at the screen.
Van/trailer users with a missing or wrong permit learn this only after the whole form, and the error has no link to the field.
Same issue as the measured contrast finding (about 3:1). Suggested 3; lowered to 2 because the tag is secondary information and the slot can still be read and booked.
The wrong-day caption shows for about 1 s on each day change; brief confusion.
Screenshot: h1 'Booked' with the red cancelled line, still followed by 'Show this at the gate'. Rare, but it can mean a wasted trip, and cancellation can be accidental (double tap).
On phones Next is a long scroll below the chosen slot; learned after one use.
Duplicates B-016/B-012. Interrupted residents lose a scarce slot without warning.
Only for forced-colours users; the 'Saturday 17 October' caption shows the chosen day.
The hold is about 5 minutes and is never mentioned; residents booking while doing something else can lose the slot and must choose again.
Suggested 4; lowered to 3 because the serious result (an accidental cancellation from a second tap) is rated under B-006, and here the effect is uncertainty for 1.5 s.
The two-day permit lead time sits behind an unlabelled (i) icon; van users can miss that they cannot book for tomorrow.
Today is the default day and same-day use is common; past slots fail only at the final step, and the error has no link back.
Duplicates B-016; the 5-minute hold is short for older residents typing their details.
Workaround via 'Change vehicle' exists but is not obvious.
Change slot resets to Today with a 'Book a slot' heading; the resident must re-find the day and trust that the other details are kept.
Suggested 1; raised to 2 because van users without a permit cannot complete the core task and must search for the application on a phone mid-booking.
A silent wrong-day booking leads to refusal at the gate and uses the weekly allowance; only the Day row on the confirm page might catch it.
Blank grid and a dead Next for 0.9 s on every day change; short-lived.
Rare (no session), but it presents a false reference as a booking.
The primary group (car owners) sees an unexplained permit field on every booking; this causes hesitation or possible abandonment by first-time older users.
A double tap, made likely by the missing pending state, silently cancels the booking and leads to refusal at the gate.
Small memory load; the details are shown again on the next step.
Suggested 4; lowered to 3 because a weekday phone route exists, so the task is delayed rather than impossible, though it means a support contact.
Duplicates B-019. Suggested 4; lowered to 3 because a phone workaround exists on weekdays.
Duplicates B-026. The permit error is late and unlinked, on a different page from the field.
Contrast of about 3:1 fails 1.4.3. Suggested 3; lowered to 2 because the tag is a secondary availability cue and the time stays readable.
One missed screen-reader announcement on first load; the count can be read in the page.
Recovery via Change slot is possible and details are kept, but it is not signposted, which is hard for screen-reader users.
Same issue as B-017: car drivers are asked for a permit they do not have.
